[package]
workspace = "../../../../../../.."
name = "semio-framework-os-services"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
rust-version.workspace = true
description = "Where tokio lives, and nowhere else. Host-side async services built ON TOP of semio-framework-async's HostAsyncRuntime/WorkerPool: the runtime impl (TokioHostRuntime, re-hosted onto the shared process-wide WorkerPool by INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b), scope table, a single host timer wheel, a bounded blocking-compute pool, an HTTP connection pool, a storage scheduler and an indexed event router. tokio is confined to this crate (sync/macros only — no owned thread pool) — its public API names only semio-framework-async types and this crate's own types, never a tokio type, exactly as wasmtime is confined behind GuestRuntime in the plugin-host crate (design ticket 26/08/17/MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME, packet R2)."

[package.metadata.semio]
role = "product"
id = "os-services"

[lints]
workspace = true

[lib]
name = "semio_framework_os_services"
path = "🦀️.rs"

[dependencies]
# 🧵️ INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b: `entrypoint` unlocks
# `semio_framework_async::block_on` — the future-polling bridge every `WorkerPool` job submitted by
# `ScopeTable::spawn_scoped`/`TimerWheel::spawn_driver`/`HttpPool::spawn_refill_driver` uses to turn
# its own worker into that task's executor (see `🦀️.rs`'s module doc), and
# `TokioHostRuntime::block_on`'s own inherent bridge delegates to directly. Workspace-internal
# feature flag on an already-present dependency, not a new third-party dependency.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
# 🎭️ MICROKERNEL-POOLED-ACTOR-PLUGIN-RUNTIME (coordinator correction on packet R2): `PackageId`
# (per-plugin quota identity) and `ActorId` (per-actor identity) are consumed from here rather than
# reinvented locally — this crate is `os-services`, not domain-neutral, so unlike
# `semio-framework-async` it should NOT keep its own parallel newtypes for the same concepts the
# actor crate already owns. Pure crate (no tokio, no threads, builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown), so
# this costs no platform coupling; `🔌️plugin/🖥️host` already depends on it the same way.
semio-framework-actor = { workspace = true }
semio-framework-job = { workspace = true }
# 🧵️ INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b: this crate no longer builds a
# `tokio::runtime::Runtime` of any flavor — `semio_framework_async::WorkerPool` (via
# `global_worker_pool`) is now the ONE owner of real OS threads a `TokioHostRuntime` and every
# service built on it schedules onto (see `🦀️.rs`'s module doc's tokio-containment note).
# The remaining tokio surface is `sync` (a pure, runtime-context-free `oneshot`/`Semaphore`/`Notify`
# — none of the three need an entered `Runtime` to function) and `macros` (the `select!` macro, also
# runtime-context-free — it is plain manual polling, not a scheduler). `rt`/`rt-multi-thread`/`time`
# are gone: their old callers (`tokio::runtime::Builder`, `tokio::task::JoinSet`,
# `tokio::time::sleep`/`sleep_until`/`timeout`) are replaced by `WorkerPool`/its `TimerWheel`
# throughout.
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["sync", "macros"] }

[dev-dependencies]
# 🧵️ INTERACTIVE-JOB-RUNTIME-REFACTOR Phase 1 packet P1b: `testkit` (and `ManualRuntime`, the
# deterministic-clock `HostAsyncRuntime` test double it gates) is DROPPED here — every test that used
# to drive `ManualRuntime`'s injected clock now drives a real `semio_framework_async::WorkerPool` on
# the real wall clock instead (`TimerWheel::spawn_driver`/`HttpPool::spawn_refill_driver` no longer
# accept a generic `R: HostAsyncRuntime` at all — see `🦀️.rs`), so nothing in this crate's
# own suite constructs a `ManualRuntime` any more. `entrypoint` is already unified in from the main
# dependency above (`cargo test` merges regular and dev-dependency features for one crate into a
# single compilation), listed again here only so this crate's OWN test suite's need for `block_on` is
# self-documenting from this line alone.
semio-framework-async = { workspace = true, features = ["entrypoint"] }
tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["sync", "macros"] }
# 🧵️ gate-services (universal-async residue sweep): every `HostAsyncRuntime` method this file's
# tests exercise is `async fn` — every test needs a real async-test harness. Path dependency, same
# pattern `🎭️actor`'s Cargo.toml already uses for this macro crate.
semio-framework-async-macros = { path = "../../../../../../🔨️modules/⏳️async/✨️macros/📦️packages/🦀️rust" }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
